Where the numbers come from

Source: vignettes/articles/provenance.Rmd
provenance.Rmd

Every number that shapes the simulated data, and its source. The simulator must not contain anything derived from CBS Remote Access microdata that has not passed CBS output checking; this inventory is the basis for confirming that. The column overview lists, per column, which generator produces it.

Levels of realism

Level Description Changes across years?
StatLine-calibrated Marginal distribution downloaded from CBS StatLine and stored in params.yaml. Updated with *_update_params(). Yes
Spine-derived Value copied from the woonbase spine, which itself is built from StatLine-calibrated parameters. Yes (via spine)
Stable per identifier Deterministic value per entity (e.g. per RINKENTEKEN) via multiplicative hashing. Year-stable — same identifier always yields the same value. No
Codelist-labelled Categorical column with hardcoded probabilities and CBS codelist labels. Plausible but not matched to any specific year. No
Random numeric Drawn from a hardcoded normal/lognormal distribution. Mean/SD are plausible but not empirically calibrated. No
Random uniform Drawn from a uniform range. Fills structural requirements only. No
Constant/template Fixed value (e.g., "R", " ", "01"). No

Sources of parameters

  • StatLine (fetched): written to params.yaml or a CSV by an *_update_params() / *_update_structure() function from public CBS StatLine tables (CC BY 4.0), so reproducible.
  • StatLine (stated, entered by hand): the file names a StatLine table, but no function fetches it.
  • Modelling choice: a documented assumption in the code.
  • Unknown: hardcoded without a documented source, listed at the end for the author to confirm.

Distributions in the YAML column specs

Columns that are not taken from the spine or from params.yaml are drawn from distributions written directly in inst/config/datasets/*/columns/*.yaml (random_categorical with probs, random_numeric with mean/sd/min/ max). Their source is not documented column by column; the column overview lists each column with its generator.

Dataset Categorical Numeric Of which via params.yaml
woonbase 32 97 0
spolis 52 70 21
inpatab 5 19 13
rdw 11 4 9
zonnestroominstallaties 4 17 2
vehtab 0 15 30 references
hoogsteopltab 10 0 2

inhatab 6 10 0
betab 4 0 3
energieverbruik 4 0 0
gba 0 2 0

Parameter files without any documented source: betab/params.yaml (business-size distribution), secmbus/params.yaml (SEC distribution), zonnestroominstallaties/params.yaml (installations, capacity, yield), burennetwerktab, colleganetwerktab, familienetwerktab (relations per person, relation-type shares).

To confirm by the author

For each item: was it taken from a public source (which), chosen as a plausible value, or computed in Remote Access? Anything computed in Remote Access must either have passed CBS output checking or be replaced before the repository is public.

  1. Woonbase defaults in R/params_woonbase.R: eigenaar_p, woningtype_p, bouwjaar_p, woz_p, opp_p, soortobj_p, vslsoort_p.
  2. .REF_TYPHH_P, .FIXED_AVG_HH_SIZE and the household-size probabilities in R/spine.R.
  3. Hand-entered parameter files: hoogsteopltab and inpatab (stated StatLine sources, but entered by hand), RDW and SPOLIS 2010-2018, energieverbruik before 2017 and solar_pv_share.
  4. Parameter files without a stated source: betab, secmbus, zonnestroominstallaties, and the three network datasets.
  5. Job and period structure in R/spolis_jobs.R and R/secm_periods.R.
  6. The hardcoded probs and mean/sd values in the YAML column specs (above), in particular the 129 in woonbase and 122 in spolis.
